text: In June of 2020 we converged. Thirty-eight of us said "the justice act," entered among us by Tim Scott on June 11, and thirty-eight said "justice in policing act," which appears in the record from June 7 under Richard E. Neal. Twenty-four of us said "unifying solutions to invigorate communities everywhere," first said by Mitch McConnell on June 17; twenty-three of us said "solutions to invigorate communities everywhere justice." Twenty-eight said "law enforcement officers," a phrase carried in the record since 2013. Twenty-four said "of george floyd," first entered by Betty McCollum on May 26, and twenty-three said "floyd justice in policing act," first said by Nancy Pelosi on June 15. Our numbers peaked together on June 25. We record that we set a bill of our naming beside a name and a bill from across the aisle, in the same days, in nearly the same counts.
